newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Agents from MI5 were today given the go ahead to help the police in fighting crime. With the act allowing MI5 spies to help the police in force, requests will be filtered through the National Criminal Intelligence Service's headquarters in Vauxhall. It is understood that the police are interested in utilising MI5's "trackers' teams of up to 16 highly trained individuals who zone in on a target and are able to follow that person anywhere.
ROWS FORCE HSBC INVESTMENT BANK CUT

HSBC, the banking giant, has cut back on its money making equity derivatives operation in London. In a substantial blow to HSBC Investment Bank it also plans to move a number of employees to other parts of the group.
NATWEST TO CUT OFF WHEELOCK FUND LINK

NatWest Markets is to concentrate on developing its fund management business through Gartmore rather than Wheelock NatWest, and is holding discussions with Wheelock about withdrawing from the fund management aspect of their partnership.
RUSSIA PLANS A GOLD EXCHANGE TO CHALLENGE WEST

The Russian authorities have decided to create a gold exchange, which will determine the gold price and allow producers to hedge output. Lev Weinberg, president of Bam Credit Bank, has been appointed chairman of the new exchange and will visit commodity experts in London to gain advice on setting it up.
